messages:
maya: Customer Amanda (acct: acmemaps) reports ~2hr window of huge tail latency + unexpected egress billing. They see a lot of traffic routed to us-east instead of eu-west and ~0.5% 401s. Ticket SUP-5124.
jack: Can you paste the sample request id / trace id and a short repro? Also which token type (api key / user token)?
maya: sent in DM: request_id=req_0a12b3c4 trace=tx-20260312-9a3b
  token type: API key (service token). Customer says they set a `Prefer-Region: eu-west` header.
  logs show: `eu-west` backend queue_depth spiked to 310, returned 429 for internal enqueue, then routing_policy=spillover kicked to `us-east`.
  customer curl repro: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" -H "Prefer-Region: eu-west" 
  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate"```
  response: `HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect -> https://us-east.api.redwood...` then `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` once hit the redirected host.
leo-oncall: Looking at metrics now — eu-west GPU pool hit 96% util @ 14:02 UTC and queue_depth jumped. Spillover policy is default `auto` with per-cluster cooldown 5m. I see ~5000 redirected requests over the hour. :eyes:
sara: Quick thought — our auth validation currently checks token region-scope on the receiving host. If redirect to other region occurs the token fails region claim check -> 401. That explains the 401s post-redirect. We probably should check token validation earlier or allow internal redirects to preserve auth validation.
jack: Can reproduce with a synthetic load locally: a tight loop of 1200 concurrent tokens causes queue growth and triggers spillover. Short repro steps in case you want to run: ```hey -n 20000 -c 1200 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" -H "Prefer-Region: eu-west" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate```
amanda-cust: confirming — we did not intentionally change anything on our side. We rely on Prefer-Region for latency isolation. We got charged for cross-region egress which surprised us.
leo-oncall: Root cause hypothesis: two bugs combinining — (1) cooldown tracked at cluster-level not per-customer/token hash, so once eu-west spilled over it kept sending same customer to us-east repeatedly during short recoveries; (2) token region-claim check runs after redirect, causing 401 when target region != token scope.
sara: Proposed quick mitigations:
  - set per-customer cooldown keyed by token hash (reduce oscillation)
  - treat `Prefer-Region` as strong hint for routing for customers with explicit header (short-term config flag)
  - on redirect allow internal auth passthrough between frontdoor and regional host (preserve Authorization header internally)
  - billing rollback / credit for accidental cross-region egress (billing team to confirm)
jack: I'll open an eng-runtime PR to: 1) compute cooldown key = sha256(token_id || customer_id), 2) increase default cooldown to 15m behind a feature flag, 3) add a proxy path that validates token claims pre-redirect.
leo-oncall: Rolling a hotfix to staging now with the per-customer cooldown change and auth passthrough flag. ETA 30m. Will run a controlled synthetic spike to ensure no oscillation.
maya: Customer updated — appreciates the quick response. They've asked for a temporary mitigation: can we pin their workspace to eu-west manually?
jack: We can patch routing for that token id to a pinned route (manual override) until fix lands. I'll apply pin for `acct:acmemaps` and confirm when done.
sara: Billing — I'll loop in finance to evaluate cross-region egress credits once we confirm counts.
leo-oncall: Update: staging hotfix shows no redirect loop on repro, and 401s eliminated when passthrough flag is enabled. Scheduling prod rollout in 45m after runbook checks. :thumbsup:
amanda-cust: Thank you, team. We'll hold on changes until you confirm.
maya: Action items: jack (pin account) DONE; leo (prod rollout) in 45m; sara (billing) to open credit evaluation; jack (PR) in flight. Closing loop after prod verification.
